rounds.text: Avana Electrosystems Ltd trades at a demanding price-to-book ratio of 6.40x against a book value of only ₹ 26.1 per share [E2], while also standing at a heavy premium with its P/B of 6.37x compared to the sector benchmark of 5.58x [E7]. This expensive valuation is entirely unsupported by tangible asset generation, evidenced by a company Return on Assets of 0%, which severely lags behind the sector benchmark of 9.71% [E8]. Furthermore, shareholders bear this rich multiple while receiving zero cash return, as the dividend yield sits firmly at 0.00% [E4]. The stock is priced for perfection, sitting 99% of the way up its 52-week range near its high of ₹ 168 [E5], despite an underlying Return on Equity of 19.84% that underperforms the sector benchmark of 23.92% [E9]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong historical median ROE of 29% over five years and 35% over three years alongside a high ROCE of 38.1% [E12, E20, E21].
